bumps in the landscape a few dozen metres long, built up of earth and stone or timber,
thousands of years ago. Some of them contain the bones of the dead,
so they might have been tombs, or churches, or... well, we don't know.

A long barrow, like any memorial, isn't built for the dead.
It's built for the living, to provide a focus point, a space to remember and to reflect.
